results.note: Adnotationes in Pentateuchon — partial translation in Victorine Texts in Translation (VTT) vol. 6 'Interpretation of Scripture: Practice' (Brepols, 2015), edited by Frans van Liere and Franklin T. Harkins.
Adnotationes in libros Regum — no English translation found despite extensive search. Work exists in PL 175.95–114 only in Latin.
Adnotatiuncula in librum Ruth — no English translation found. This brief annotation on Ruth (37 words) appears not to have been translated.
Adnotatiunculae in Joelem — no English translation found despite search. Work in PL 175.321–372 remains in Latin only.
Adnotatiunculae in Threnos — no English translation found. Biblical annotation on Lamentations (26,080 words) not yet translated to English.
Adnotatiunculae in librum Judicum — no English translation found despite search. Brief annotation on Judges (3,623 words) remains untranslated.
De V septenis (De quinque septenis) — English translation by Andrew Dunning published in Scholarly Editing (2016), with Latin text edited from Paris MS 717.

De scripturis et scriptoribus sacris — machine-assisted English translation (ChatGPT + human editing) available at threepillarsblog.org (2023), but translator notes it had not been formally translated before. Status ambiguous: blog translation vs. formal scholarly edition.
Explanatio in Canticum B. Mariae — no English translation found. Magnificat commentary exists in Latin (PL 175.413–432) but no published English version located.
Expositio in Abdiam — no English translation found. Commentary on Obadiah (PL 175.371–406) remains in Latin only.
Expositio in Hierarchiam Coelestem S. Dionysii — no English translation found despite extensive search. Major commentary on Pseudo-Dionysius (89,106 words; PL 175.923–1154) remains untranslated.

Homiliae in Ecclesiasten — partial English translation exists (excerpt in 1962 Selected Spiritual Writings); VTT volumes reference selections. Full work status unclear; may contain untranslated portions.
Quaestiones in Epistolas Pauli — attributed to pseudo-Hugonian (later Victorine author, not Hugh himself per scholarly consensus). No English translation found for this work.

De amore sponsi ad sponsam — English translation by 'A Religious of C.S.M.V.' in 1962 Selected Spiritual Writings (Wipf & Stock reprint 2009); also in Victorine Texts in Translation vol. 2 'On Love' (Brepols, 2011).

De arca Noe morali — complete English translation by 'A Religious of C.S.M.V.' in 1962 Selected Spiritual Writings (Wipf & Stock 2009); also in VTT vol. 5 'Spiritual Formation and Mystical Symbolism' (Brepols, 2022).
De arca Noe mystica — English translation in VTT vol. 5 'Spiritual Formation and Mystical Symbolism' (Brepols, 2022) as 'A Short Treatise on the Form of the Ark'.
De artificio meditandi — French translation by Roger Baron in 'Six Opuscules Spirituels' (Les Éditions du Cerf, 1969, pp. 44–59). No confirmed complete English translation found.
De fructibus carnis et spiritus — no English translation found despite search. Small treatise (2,971 words) remains in Latin only.
De institutione novitiorum — first English translation published by Brepols in VTT vol. 9 'Life at Saint Victor' (2021), edited by Frans van Liere and Juliet Mousseau.
De laude charitatis — English translation ('On the Praise of Charity') translated by A.B. Kraebel in Victorine Texts in Translation vol. 2 'On Love' (Brepols, 2011).

De modo orandi — no complete English translation found. French translation by Roger Baron ('Six Opuscules Spirituels', 1969) exists; Spanish-Latin bilingual versions documented but no confirmed full English translation.
De potestate et voluntate Dei — no English translation found. Very brief treatise (841 words) on divine power and will remains untranslated.
De quatuor voluntatibus in Christo — no English translation found despite search. Treatise on Christ's four wills (1,840 words) remains in Latin only.
De sacramentis legis naturalis et scriptae — no standalone English translation found. May be included in broader sacramental collections but no specific translation confirmed.

De sacramentis — complete English translations available: Roy Deferrari (Mediaeval Academy of America, 1951); also VTT vol. 10 'On the Sacraments' selections (Brepols, 2020) edited by Hugh Feiss, OSB.
De sapientia animae Christi — no English translation found. Treatise on Christ's soul's wisdom (4,538 words) remains untranslated.
De vanitate mundi — partial English translation (Books I–II only, not complete work) by 'A Religious of C.S.M.V.' in 1962 Selected Spiritual Writings (Wipf & Stock reprint 2009).
De virginitate B. Mariae — no English translation found despite search. Treatise on the Virgin Mary's virginity (8,143 words) remains in Latin only.
Epistolae — no complete English translation found. Hugh's letters (2,417 words total) remain in Patrologia Latina only; individual letters may appear in scholarly articles.

Eruditio didascalica (Didascalicon) — complete English translation by Jerome Taylor (Columbia University Press, 1961); multiple modern editions and Brepols VTT vol. 3 'Interpretation of Scripture: Theory' (2012) includes selections.
Expositio in regulam S. Augustini — now attributed to Victorine school (not Hugh himself). Very old printed Latin edition (Bruges, 1697) exists; no modern English translation found.
Institutiones in Decalogum — no English translation found despite search. Brief treatise on the Ten Commandments (3,441 words) remains untranslated.

Soliloquium de arrha animae — partial English translation in 1962 Selected Spiritual Writings (Wipf & Stock 2009); French translation by Feiss/Sicard. Full English translation of complete work not confirmed.

Summa sententiarum — attributed to pseudo-Hugonian (NOT authentic Hugh; scholarly consensus denies authorship). Partial English translation of sections I.15–19 by Joshua Benson published with introduction.
